method: Parallax is the horizontal separation of the left and right images of a point at the sensor, and the page computes it from the pinhole projection of a converged stereo rig. The focal length is first expressed in pixels as focal length divided by sensor width times the horizontal resolution, so a 35 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor at 1920 pixels across is 1866.67 pixels. The separation is that pixel focal length times the interaxial in metres times the difference between the reciprocal of the subject distance and the reciprocal of the convergence distance, which is the same as shifting each camera's image horizontally so that points at the convergence distance carry zero disparity. A subject nearer than the convergence distance therefore returns crossed parallax and sits in front of the screen plane; a subject beyond it returns uncrossed parallax and sits behind. The share of frame width is the absolute separation divided by the horizontal resolution, and the budget is entered as a percentage of that width. The near limit solves the same relation at positive budget, the far limit solves it at negative budget and is reported as no limit when the budget is wider than the convergence term, because uncrossed parallax then never reaches it at any distance. The largest interaxial is the baseline that puts this subject exactly on the budget. A zero interaxial is accepted and reported as no stereo separation with no limits. Focal lengths of 4 to 300 mm, sensor widths of 3 to 70 mm, resolutions of 320 to 8192 whole pixels, interaxials of 0 to 500 mm, convergence distances of 0.3 to 200 m, subject distances of 0.2 to 500 m and budgets of 0.05 to 5 percent are accepted; blanks, words, negatives, exponent notation and more than three decimal places are refused with the field named, and the horizontal field of view is reported from the same triangle as a check on the lens and sensor entries. The model assumes a parallel, converged rig with rectilinear lenses: toe-in, lens distortion, rolling shutter, floating windows, projection screen size and viewing distance are not modelled, and the comfortable budget for a real presentation depends on all of them. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
